clue.text: Doctor's father getting aid in a trice — all wrong

parts.note: pa is an everyday word for a father

indicators.note: all wrong says the letters of these words are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's dad manages to get medical help in no time, but everything goes awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all wrong' rearranges AIDINATRICE into EDIATRICIAN, which follows PA. The 's of 'Doctor's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A paediatrician is a physician who specialises in treating children.

parts.note: an ace is someone outstanding; ace as an adjective means excellent
tat is cheap, worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a European art film as superb rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a transparent plastic sheet, a kind of film used for overhead projectors and photography.

definitions.meaning: to walk out with someone is an old phrase for courting them
the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: Courting while carrying a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to go on romantic outings with them, and the palm's sweet brown fruit shares the same name.

clue.text: After a party, little chap's shamefaced

indicators.note: after says the little chap comes following the a and the party

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party
Ed is a short form of a boy's name, Edward or Edmund, so a little chap

explanation.surface: After a party, a small boy looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little chap' is a shortened name: ED, the pet form of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed or ashamed, just as shamefaced does.

clue.text: Platform shoes finally found in rubbish — odd

indicators.note: found in says the last letter of shoes sits inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word shoes

parts.note: rum is a British word meaning odd or strange

explanation.surface: Platform shoes turned up among the rubbish, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform shoes' looks like a fashion phrase, but 'Platform' alone is the definition. 'found in' puts S, the last letter of 'shoes', inside ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand from which a speaker addresses an audience.

parts.note: Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary in crosswords

indicators.note: for starters asks for the first letter, the start, of the word food

explanation.surface: A cook serves revolutionary dishes as the opening course.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary of the Cuban revolution, gives CHE; 'for starters' takes F from 'food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially one in charge of a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Book has a city gent in it on cocaine

indicators.note: in it says the gent goes inside the city just named

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the city most often abbreviated in crosswords
a gent is a man
C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: A book about a city gentleman who takes cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city gent' reads as one phrase, a City of London businessman, but splits: LA is the city and MAN the gent, with MAN placed 'in it'. C goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication of calendars, tables and facts.

clue.text: When drunk, nab carved lion dish

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and mixed up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk grabs a carved stone lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When drunk' scrambles NAB CARVED LION; 'carved' looks like the clue's verb but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver and bacon is a traditional British meal of fried liver served with bacon.

clue.text: Action may have led to one being accommodated in camp

definitions.text: Action may have led to one being accommodated in camp

parts.words: Action may have led to one being accommodated in camp
parts.note: the action is military combat, and the camp is a guarded compound where a captured soldier is held, not a holiday site

explanation.surface: Something someone did ended with a stay at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' suggests a holiday camp and 'Action' any deed; read them as battle and a detention camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier captured in battle is held in a guarded enemy camp until released.

indicators.note: aboard says the answer is on board, carried inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: On a cruise liner, the tiara-wearing passengers are bored.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in liNER TIAras.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is lethargy, a lack of energy to act, which is close to bored listlessness.

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the flag word

parts.note: a streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant

explanation.surface: The ship's flag is flying incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' reads as 'incorrect', but tells you to drop R from STREAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a vessel powered by a steam engine.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Test returned, marks cut' (4) as held: EXAM reversed is MAXE, and no word for 'marks' cut short gives MAXE; the OCR text seems to misread a word and no source gives the printed clue.

parts.note: the clue asks for the word that completes 'look ...' as a phrase meaning hurry up; 'this way' points to that word

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dawdler to get a move on and turn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look this way' sounds like a photographer's call; it means 'look' followed by the answer, the British phrase 'look sharp', which is an order to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is an idiom telling someone to be quick and alert.

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: birds twitter when they sing, so twittered means sung

explanation.surface: Someone tweeted all about animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus are wildebeest, large African antelopes.

indicators.note: accepts says the word for lad takes in the books, holding them inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
OT is the Old Testament, the usual crossword books

explanation.surface: A boy receives books as an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is plunder, valuable things seized as winnings.

indicators.note: in the ear says the word is as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with a fleece

explanation.surface: Someone has a vertical cut on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the ear' looks like the place of the cut; it says SHEAR is heard as SHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer cliff is perpendicular, rising straight up.

indicators.note: about means moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor has no idea about some dead tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOIDEA into ADENOI, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are a mass of lymphatic tissue at the back of the nose.

indicators.note: about says the complaint word goes around the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is Latin, the classical language, for this

explanation.surface: Moaning about a hairstyle from the classical era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical' points to Latin: HIC means 'this'. MOAN goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a hairstyle with a central strip of upright hair and shaved sides.

clue.text: About time jagged tear in middle of teddy's darned

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the middle of teddy's
middle of takes the central letters of teddy's
about says the rearranged tear goes around the time letter
jagged means torn and ragged, so the letters of the word tear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Just in time, a tear in the middle of a teddy bear has been mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darned' looks like the mended teddy, but means 'confounded'. 'jagged' turns TEAR into RATE; 'About' puts it around T for RATTE, which goes 'in' DD, the middle letters of 'teddy's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild curse words meaning blasted or confounded.

clue.text: A star, embarrassed when set up in parts

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means lifted, so the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: red-faced, someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: A star blushes when caught out in parts of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses RED to DER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart, into separate pieces.

clue.text: Put down heart of rising in military HQ

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the military headquarters

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letters of the word rising

explanation.surface: Someone suppresses an uprising inside army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests crushing the rising; it means lay down. SI, the middle of 'rising', goes 'in' DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to lay something down or set it in place.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Declare, putting England (7)' as held is cut short: AVER around ENG fits, but the clue holds no insertion indicator and no definition, and no source gives the rest.

indicators.note: different says these letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hoot is another kind of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges IS A HOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the noise of a sneeze, written out.

clue.text: Gentle doctor perhaps wasting time and energy on student

indicators.note: wasting says letters are lost from the word for doctor perhaps

parts.note: a doctor holds a degree, so a doctor is an example of a graduate
E is the physics symbol for energy
L is for learner, the student of a British driving L-plate

explanation.surface: A kindly doctor is wasting time and energy on a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor perhaps' is a graduate; 'wasting' drops T and E from GRADUATE for GRADUA, and L, a learner driver's plate in Britain, goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual slope is gentle, rising little by little.

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out

parts.note: muzzy means hazy or unclear, so vague

explanation.surface: Feeling feverish and fuzzy-headed, though not badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' reads as 'only slightly' but drops V from VAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old name for malarial fever with shivering fits.

parts.note: a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A special suit made for a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is an old word for a youth or young lad, a scion of a family.

clue.text: Vulgar fellow in buff running back

indicators.note: running back says the result runs backwards
in says the fellow letter goes inside the buff word

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: A coarse man in the nude is running back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in buff' suggests naked, but buff is FAN. F goes 'in' it for FFAN, which 'running back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky, lacking style or taste.

indicators.note: overthrow of means turning over, so the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: deps is a short form of deputies

explanation.surface: The deputies were swiftly toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow' reads as a coup but reverses DEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, meaning moved quickly.

indicators.note: on one's tongue says the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: to fly is to flee, run away

explanation.surface: An insect, a fly, lands on someone's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a second insect; it is the verb, to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small jumping parasitic insect.

parts.note: the clue reads as a mother-in-law, but this man's wife was also his own mother, in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A man's mother-in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the king of Thebes unknowingly married his mother Jocasta, so his wife is his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theban king of Sophocles' tragedy married Jocasta, unaware she was his mother.

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an ell is an old measure of length
UVA is ultraviolet A, harmful rays from the sun

explanation.surface: Extremely hot weather means measuring the harmful sun rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very hot' reads together, but 'Very' is the definition. An ELL was an old cloth measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Helluva is informal for 'hell of a', used as an intensifier meaning extremely.

clue.text: Friend pursuing belief in the old way

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the friend word comes after the belief word

parts.note: a tradition is a belief handed down
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend chasing an old-fashioned faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally means according to custom, the long-established manner.
